agent.problem: Too much of stop 1 depends on discovery guesses rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 4, 6, 9 and 14 ask for Mount Seir, the direction north, the fear of Esau's descendants, God's reason for withholding their land and the next road without giving the baker a basis to infer those answers. That is five of the stop's eight choices, so this stop becomes more of a guessing game than the allowed occasional discovery question.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Deuteronomy 2:11 is skipped entirely. The baker is never told that the Emites, like the Anakites, were regarded as Rephaim. Besides losing that part of Moses' historical note, this leaves 'land of the Rephaim too' in card 17 without the earlier description that 'too' points back to.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

human.problem: In the BSB, Deuteronomy 2:10-12 and 2:20-23 are set in parentheses as background notes about earlier peoples. Verse 12 looks back on Israel's settlement in its land as already done ('just as Israel did in the land'). Even so, card 4 says 'Moses drops in a side note,' card 7 says 'Moses compares,' and card 19 says 'Moses says the LORD did the same.' Each one names Moses as the speaker of these notes. Cards 17 and 20 call them 'side note' and 'last note' without naming a speaker.
human.question: Can Papa Dorin say Moses speaks the bracketed background notes in Deuteronomy 2:10-12 and 2:20-23? Or should he leave the speaker open, the way cards 17 and 20 do? The 'Leave open what the text leaves open' rule covers who is being spoken to, why, and how two things connect. It doesn't say how to handle bracketed asides inside a speech.

human.problem: In the BSB, 2:10-12 and 2:20-23 are set off in parentheses as background notes. Verse 2:12 speaks of what Israel did "in the land that the LORD gave them" in the past tense, before Israel had entered the land. Cards 4, 7 and 19 credit these notes to Moses ("Moses drops in a side note," "Moses compares," "Moses says"). Cards 17 and 20 call them notes without naming a speaker.
human.question: Should Papa Dorin credit the parenthetical background notes in Deuteronomy 2 to Moses, or leave the speaker open, as the cards on 2:20-23 do?

human.problem: The joke invites the baker to say "Zamzummites" out loud because of how the name sounds. It isn't a put-down, but the joke is about a people's name, not about their human situation.
human.question: Are jokes about how the name of a people in Scripture sounds acceptable under the reverence and no-put-downs rules?
